This may be your downfall. I don't know what your design thoughts are such that your game needs three different (two only slightly different?) battle systems, but trying to code additional mechanics that will correctly fit all three of those may get very complicated.
Khyoshyro said:
However, what I did only works individually (each character benefits from their own counter, instead of everyone having a common counter)
Click to expand...
Because that's how you made it.
You should be putting the state on the
enemy
, and doing all of the combo stacks on the
target
, not the user.
I don't get what you're doing in the remove effect. There's no point in clamping from 1 to 1, just set whatever you want...to 1. But I don't know why you want anything set to 1 anyway. You should just be deleting the comboStack and that's all the notetag needs.
I also don't see the point of the troop events. You make your attacks apply this state to the target, then you make your enemy's skills remove the state from themselves - thus clearing the stacks.

posts.body:
You don't need anything inside the Custom Remove Effect except
Code:
delete target._comboStacks;
You also don't want most of the stuff in that Custom Confirm Effect. If you have all your attacks adding the state, most of it will be done in the Custom Apply.
Code:
<Custom Confirm Effect>
if (this.isPhysical() && value > 0 && target._comboStacks)
    value *= 1 + target._comboStacks * .01;
</Custom Confirm Effect>

posts.author: Khyoshyro
Robro33
posts.body:
Khyoshyro said:
<Custom Confirm Effect>
Click to expand...
confirm effects are triggered when the battler with the state takes action. if that state is on an enemy and youre trying to make it so that something happens when they get hit, your code isnt doing anything in that regard. if youre increasing the damage the affected battler takes and youre using their own _comboStacks property, you realistically should be using a react effect, not a confirm one.
Khyoshyro said:
the hitcounter dont increace with successive hits
Click to expand...
you didnt tell it to. in your apply effect, you used setStateCounter() to set the state's counter. the counter only updates when you call it. if you want it to update after every hit, then you need to tell it to after every hit. that would go in the react effect, or you call the apply effect
Khyoshyro said:
and each hit isnt increased by 1%
Click to expand...
youre not incrementing the _comboStacks property anywhere. you set the property when the state is applied, but you never said anywhere that it should increase after a hit. that too goes in the react effect, or the skill's own tags and then also update the counter
Khyoshyro said:
var stacks = target._comboStacks.clamp(0, 1000);
Click to expand...
that only gets ran when the state is applied. unless the battler is getting the state applied to them numerous times while already active, your clamp isnt going to do anything.
if they didnt have the state before, then youve set it to 0. if you are applying the state to a battler that already has it, then the value is retained and will be clamped *only on application*. unless every hit they take applies the state (which then clamps the value), it makes more sense to me to move it to where the incrementing happens.

Applying a state when you hit with a skill is one of the basic settings in RPG Maker. You want to be familiar with all of these database settings and event commands before you try to do things with plugins and code.

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
Khyoshyro said:
but ennemies are the user of the state
Click to expand...
Khyoshyro said:
Then the ennemi muqt be the target of this state "in game" but the user of the code
Click to expand...
when youre working with the notetags provided by the buffs and states plugin, all of the notetags that fall under the category of "Custom Action Effects" use the action's perspective.
the user is whoever is using the skill and the target is who's getting the skill. so even if the state is on Battler A, "user" within the react effect will always mean some
other
battler unless Battler A is using a skill on themself.
in the "Custom Timing Effect" notetags like apply and remove, the user and the target are both whoever has the state on them and are interchangeable.

there is only one ..."weir" thing : some totally abnormal and incredibly high damage is inflicted on the enemy, as the next record show:

its not high damage, the damage just isnt an integer. the MV damage popup sheet doesnt have a spot for a decimal point, but theres a small space for where it would be. if youve noticed, the first hit you did 62 damage, but every single hit that followed it had shown 2 separate numbers. you need to round the damage. damage calculated through a skill damage formula automatically does so, but additional damage from notetags like that need to be rounded.

value *= 1 + target._comboStacks * .01;

Code:
value += Math.ceil(value * target._comboStacks * .01);
